home.headline: Ole Miss' Kewan Lacy explains how he can run so strong even though he keeps getting injured
home.blurb: Lacy was limited with an injury, but neither it nor the Tigers defense kept him down. Despite a suffering what the SEC Network TV broadcast said was a lower-body injury and missing much of the second quarter, Lacy rushed for 122 yards on 16 carries. Lacy rotated between the medical tent and the exercise bike on the Ole Miss sideline in the second quarter. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding did not give specifics, but said it was a different injury than the left shoulder injury Lacy entered the game with. That injury prevented him from playing in Week 4 vs Florida and, after an open week, limited his availability in Week 6 vs Vanderbilt. Lacy's toughness has been established. He led the nation in carries in 2025 and got offseason surgery on his left shoulder. That same shoulder kept getting banged up, and the new lower-body pain he got courtesy of the Missouri game isn't enough to keep him out. "Kewan wants to play," Golding said. "He's put a lot into this. He's super competitive. I looked up and it was the fourth and said, 'Get Kewan's ass out of the game.' But that's him, 'Coach, put me in.'" OXFORD — Ole Miss football running back Kewan Lacy has had to set his alarm earlier this season. Because of injuries, he's been a regular on the midweek SEC injury reports. His weeks starring beside quarterback Trinidad Chambliss in the Ole Miss backfield have been filled with getting treatment to ensure he can suit up on game day. "You get up early," Lacy said. "Long nights, long days. But, you know, if you really love football then you're going to make time." No. 10 Ole Miss beat No. 13 Missouri 31-3 at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Lacy was a key part of the dominating performance. "I'm doing good," Lacy said after the game. It was Ole Miss coach Pete Golding who decided to start leaning on backup running back Makhi Frazier in the fourth quarter. Lacy has been less than 100% since a Week 1 win against Louisville. Lacy has rushed for 352 yards and five touchdowns. He is averaging 5.7 yards per carry. Chambliss said Lacy has been a regular visitor to the training room. "He's extremely tough," Chambliss said. "I don't think all year he's been healthy throughout the year. He's pushing through. Being a running back, that's tough. You're going to hit a lot. His toughness is wild. It's insane." Golding said no injuries from the Missouri game are expected to be permanent disruptions to the season. Lacy will continue on his treatment plan before Ole Miss' next game at No. 6 Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) on Oct. 24 (6:30 p.m., ABC). "It's part of the game, nicks and bruises," Lacy said. "You've just got to attack whatever you're doing. Rehab, practice, whatever you're doing." Sam Hutchens covers Ole Miss for the Clarion Ledger. On the initial report released Wednesday evening, at least 15 players that have been starters or regular contributors were listed either as questionable or probable — six on offense and another nine on defense. Brett Norfleet , a senior tight end who's started three games this year, was questionable on Wednesday, doubtful on Thursday, questionable on Friday then deemed a game-time decision on Saturday. He ultimately did not play after going through warmups. Jeremiah Beasley , part of the second-string linebacking group, followed the same path as Norfleet: questionable on Wednesday, doubtful on Thursday, questionable on Friday, then a game-time decision on Saturday. Robert Woodyard Jr. , questionable on both Wednesday and Thursday, probable on Friday, then off the list by Saturday, ultimately started and played 42 snaps at middle linebacker against the Rebels, but recorded just one tackle. "Going to depend on how he recovers," Drinkwitz said when asked for more details. "We'll see. I don't know yet. As usual, the game has ACC and national title race implications , though this season those conversations are focused far more on the Hurricanes, who finished last season as the national runner-up and is currently the heavy favorite to win the ACC in 2026. Things are far different for Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell, who entered the year facing serious job pressure and now risks falling to 3-4 on the season and 1-3 in ACC play if the Seminoles cannot pull a stunning upset. Wins against Miami in 2021, 2022 and 2023 were crucial building blocks of Norvell's eventual ACC Championship run, but now it's Mario Cristobal who has the chance to string together three straight wins in the series after the Hurricanes got the better of Florida State in 2024 and 2025. The return to Miami Gardens also spotlights what has become a notable home-field advantage for Miami in this recent run, as the Hurricanes are 15-1 at home since the start of the 2024 season, including that 36-14 win against the Seminoles in Hard Rock Stadium two years ago. Miami has been absolute rock stars in the ACC and the sport as a whole, continuing the momentum from the team's College Football Playoff run with eye-popping scores and stat-stuffing performances to start the 2026 season. away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: Ashton Daniels kneeled out the clock, and we're headed to overtime. The teams will alternate possessions starting at the opponents' 25-yard line. If it goes to a second overtime, teams will have to go for 2 if they score a touchdown. After that, the teams will trade 2-point conversion tries until there's a winner. In his first game back since the opener at Stanford, cornerback Xavier Lucas made what could turn out to be the biggest play of the game. Tre Wisner got loose on a long run, but Ethan O'Connor stripped the ball loose, sending the ball skidding across the wet grass. Lucas fell on it to give Miami the ball at its own 39. Darian Mensah may not be having his best game, but he is still showing impeccable touch on some difficult throws. He got a throw out just before Rylan Kennedy could get to him, lofting a 19-yard looper to Vandrevius Jacobs. As the fourth quarter begins, the Canes have the ball at the FSU 20. Miami outgained FSU 149-76 in the third quarter, but the visitors benefitted big time on two turnovers (one on downs). UM can't afford to miss here if they want to stay undefeated. One play after Ousmane Kromah was carted to the locker room with a devastating ankle injury, Ashton Daniels took it in himself for the game-tying touchdown from 2 yards out. He held up three and two fingers to shout out Kromah's number 32 after the score. With FSU driving again and the 2-minute timeout having just passed, Chase Smith wrapped up Ousmane Kromah by the ankles. The running back was injured on the play, and trainers brought out an air cast for him. He was carted off the field. The Seminoles were already without Sam Singleton Jr. entering the game; without Kromah, among the top-20 running backs in the nation with 565 yards entering the game, Texas transfer Tre Wisner becomes their main RB. After a Miami three-and-out, Ashton Daniels returned to the game and looked like he didn't miss a beat, scrambling for 10 yards on a third-and-8. Ashton Daniels scrambled for 14 yards. As he slid, safety Zechariah Poyser hit him in the head area, bringing out a flag for the personal foul. His ejection for targeting was upheld upon review. That play and Bryce Fitzgerald's injury leaves an already depleted Miami secondary without two more starters. Xavier Lucas got injured in the opener vs. Stanford and hasn't played since, but he's expected to be back in the starting lineup tonight. O.J. Frederique also has been out since Week 1 but needs more time to return, leaving either Damari Brown, Ethan O'Connor or converted safety Bryce Fitzgerald starting opposite Lucas against FSU. Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Kentucky vs. Oklahoma game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction chrisbeasmore Mon, October 12, 2026 at 2:11 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky's offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners' other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners' stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer's primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners' running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . ESPN gives Kentucky a 32.1% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 5-1 under first-year head coach Will Stein after a huge upset over LSU, while Oklahoma is coming off a rivalry win over Texas. Both teams could experience an emotional hangover after their big victories, but I believe Kentucky can overcome that challenge and earn another road win. Despite concerns about linebacker injuries, the Wildcats have a chance to improve to 6-1, become bowl-eligible, and remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. Final Score: Kentucky 31, Oklahoma 20. How do you see this one playing out?

Two teams coming off massive upset victories will collide Saturday night as No. 15 Kentucky (5-1) travels to Norman to face Oklahoma (3-2) in a crucial SEC matchup. Kentucky is coming off a thrilling 35-34 overtime victory over LSU, while Oklahoma stunned Texas 27-24 in the Red River Rivalry. Both programs have plenty to prove, but the biggest question is whether Oklahoma can build on its impressive victory and finally establish some consistency. Kentucky: Can the Wildcats Keep Rolling? Kentucky has been one of the SEC's biggest surprises under first-year head coach Will Stein. Quarterback Kenny Minchey has thrown for 1,394 yards and 11 touchdowns, while running back CJ Baxter has rushed for 484 yards and eight scores. Baxter was outstanding against LSU, rushing for 123 yards and two touchdowns. The Wildcats are averaging nearly 35 points per game, but Oklahoma's defense presents a completely different challenge. Brent Venables has built one of the nation's most physical defensive units, allowing just 17.6 points and approximately 267 yards per game. If Kentucky cannot establish Baxter early, Minchey could face constant pressure throughout the evening. Oklahoma: The Defense Is Carrying This Team Oklahoma's victory over Texas was impressive, but the Sooners still have serious offensive concerns. Quarterback John Mateer has thrown for 1,038 yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Against Texas, Mateer managed just 155 passing yards, and Oklahoma needed a blocked punt touchdown and multiple defensive stops to secure the victory. However, the Sooners' defense has been outstanding. Oklahoma is allowing just 150 passing yards per game, making life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. With Adepoju Adebawore creating pressure up front, the Sooners have the personnel to disrupt Kentucky's offense. If Mateer can avoid turnovers and Oklahoma establishes any consistency running the football, the Sooners should have enough offensive production to win. How Each Team Wins Kentucky must establish Baxter early, protect Minchey, and avoid giving Oklahoma short fields through turnovers. The Wildcats also need to force Mateer into obvious passing situations. For Oklahoma, everything starts defensively. The Sooners must contain Baxter, pressure Minchey, and create opportunities for their offense. Playing in Norman should also provide a significant advantage for Venables' team. I expect Kentucky to keep this game competitive, but Oklahoma's defense will ultimately make the difference. The Wildcats should find some success moving the football, particularly early, but sustaining long drives against this Sooners defense will be extremely difficult. Mateer won't need to deliver a spectacular performance. Instead, Oklahoma will rely on its defense, field position, and a few explosive offensive plays. Expect Kentucky to threaten late before Oklahoma comes up with one final defensive stop. Final Score: Oklahoma 27, No. 15 Kentucky 21 The Sooners build on their Red River victory, improve to 4-2, and keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Sooners host No. 15/17 Kentucky on Saturday at 6:30 p.m. in Norman, and the setup could not be much cleaner for a measuring-stick home opener in SEC play. Oklahoma is 3-2 and 1-1 after knocking off No. 1 Texas on a walk-off field goal. Kentucky is 5-1 and 3-1 after beating No. 10 LSU in overtime. Both teams are coming in hot. Only one of them gets to leave Norman still feeling like the week actually changed something. That is the whole tone of this game. Oklahoma does not need another moral victory. It already got the statement result in the Cotton Bowl. Now the question is whether Brent Venables ' team can stack a second one against a ranked opponent at home, in throwbacks, with the building expecting the version of the Sooners that showed up after halftime in Dallas. The storyline writes itself. Oklahoma just beat the top team in the country. Kentucky just survived LSU 35-34 in overtime for its second straight 35-34 overtime win. Will Stein's group is not sneaking into Norman quietly. This is Kentucky's highest AP ranking since 2022, and the Wildcats are playing with the kind of confidence that makes road environments less intimidating than they used to be. Stein's background adds a little spice too. He was on Texas' staff from 2015 to 2017, then spent the last three years as Oregon's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach while the Ducks made the College Football Playoff. He knows big stages. More importantly for Saturday, he has a quarterback in Kenny Minchey who takes care of the ball, extends plays, and has already shown he can finish tight games. Oklahom a's recent history after Texas also hangs over the night. Since 1999, the Sooners are 25-2 in the game immediately following the Red River rivalry. The only losses in that stretch were to Kansas State in 2014 and South Carolina in 2024. That is a real trend, but trends do not tackle Minchey or cover Kentucky's skill players. Oklahoma still has to earn the next one. If the Sooners are going to control this game, it starts where most of their best football has started all year: on defense. Oklahoma is allowing just 12.8 first downs per game, best in the country. The Sooners also rank among the national leaders in third-down defense, red-zone defense, passing defense, total defense, and sacks. Opponents have scored on only 15 of 62 possessions. The second-half numbers are even tighter. Oklahoma has given up just 27 points after halftime all season, including only three in the third quarter. That profile matters against a quarterback like Minchey. He is efficient, hard to rattle, and dangerous when the pocket breaks down. Oklahoma cannot afford soft edges or impatient linebackers. The formula is the same one that showed up against Texas: keep contain, force longer developing throws, win early downs, and make Kentucky drive the hard way. The Sooners are 11-2 under Venables when they score a defensive touchdown, including 4-0 since the start of last season. They do not need another pick-six Saturday. They do need the same disruptive identity. The personnel is built for it too. All 14 defensive starters began their college careers at Oklahoma. Owen Heinecke has been the tone-setter again, leading the team in tackles in four of five games. Peyton Bowen just took over a rivalry game. Courtland Guillory made the late interception that set up the Texas winner. The front still has Taylor Wein, David Stone, Danny Okoye, and enough depth to keep the pressure coming. If that group plays clean, Oklahoma has a real chance to dictate the night. The uncomfortable truth is that Oklahoma's offense is still looking for consistency even after the biggest win of the season. The Texas game gave the Sooners a blueprint more than a finished product. They scored in all three phases, finally got some second-half juice on the ground through Lloyd Avant, and did just enough in the passing game when the moment arrived. John Mateer did not have to play hero ball. Isaiah Sategna still created the biggest throws on the final drive. Rocky Beers continues to look like one of the smarter portal additions on the roster, ranking among the national leaders in receiving yards per game by a tight end. That is the version Oklahoma needs again. Not perfect. Just complementary. The red-zone efficiency has been solid, and the explosive pass plays are still there. What has lagged is the ability to stay on schedule without leaning so hard on the defense and special teams. Kentucky's defense has not been elite by the numbers, but Venables already made clear that "relief" is not the word inside the building. Every week is still about Oklahoma getting better. The offensive line remains one of the quieter swing factors. Michael Fasusi has been working back from the shoulder injury that knocked him out after the opener, and any step toward getting the line more whole helps the whole operation. Avant gave the run game a pulse against Texas. Xavier Robinson and Tory Blaylock still have to become more reliable pieces if Oklahoma wants drives that do not feel like they are always one negative play from stalling. There are plenty of side notes around the game, and most of them favor the home team if Oklahoma plays like it should. The Sooners are wearing the Bud Wilkinson-era throwbacks again. Memorial Stadium has been a fortress since 1999, with a 153-17 record and a sellout streak that never seems to blink. Venables is 2-2 in conference home openers. The roster has true veteran captains across both sides of the ball. Special teams, once a liability, now look like a genuine strength with Tate Sandell , Grayson Miller, and Doug Deakin's unit playing with confidence. But the schedule context is what keeps this from feeling comfortable. Oklahoma has already seen Michigan, Georgia, and Texas. Still left are Kentucky, Mississippi State, Ole Miss, and Missouri among the ranked or dangerous remaining names. This is not a soft landing after Dallas. It is the next hard one. Kentucky is good enough to punish a flat home team, especially if Minchey gets into a rhythm and Oklahoma's offense stalls early. That is why Saturday matters beyond one week in the standings. The Texas win stopped the spiral and put Oklahoma back in the conversation. A home win over a ranked Kentucky team would make that conversation real. A letdown would turn Dallas back into an isolated highlight instead of the start of a run. The Sooners do not need to look perfect. They need to look intentional. Defend with the same edge that has carried them all year. Run the ball well enough to keep the game clean. Let Mateer manage instead of force. Protect the edges against Minchey. And finish the night like a team that understands the standard is no longer just competing in these games. Oklahoma has the defense. It has the home field. It has the momentum. Kentucky has the confidence of a team that has already won a couple of ugly, important games. Saturday night in Norman should tell us which one is actually building something.

away.headline: Oklahoma vs. Kentucky Injury Report: Sooners offensive line banged up
away.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. home.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , following us on Twitter/X , and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. Published Oct 14, 2026 ADAM CARRIKER Adam’s dream of playing for the Huskers came to fruition. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. This is the season for an Oregon team that should be in full rock-and-roll mode at this point, but instead it's been one big, sad trombone of a season. The Ducks are still 3-2 with a not-that-horrible schedule the rest of the way outside of a trip to Ohio State. They lost to UCLA, but they can stay alive in the Big Ten title hunt with one more loss, even if an at-large CFP bid is likely gone with a third defeat and no Big Ten Championship. And they have to do it with Nebraska's former star quarterback, Dylan Raiola – maybe. Nebraska had Indiana cooked, but it turned the stove off too early. The Hoosiers rallied back for a 20-17 win, but that might have been more about the defending national champs not being as good this year than the Huskers being close to fantastic. However, winning in Eugene is still hard, and if Nebraska can do it, it's 6-1 with a favorable schedule – Ohio State comes to Lincoln – and all of a sudden, it's on the fast track to 10-2 – at least – and a possible at-large CFP bid. Nebraska vs Oregon: Quick Hits Oregon ends a good run of home games and goes to Illinois after this. After that, it hosts Northwestern before going to Ohio State. Nebraska starts a run of three road games in four dates, getting a week off before playing Washington, and then it's off to Illinois. The two have never played as Big Ten teams. Oregon won the last meeting 42-35 in 2017. The Huskers are 6-2 overall in the series, with the first win in 1952. How To Watch Nebraska vs Oregon Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 11:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Nebraska Will Win UCLA beat up, battered, and bruised Oregon last week. The Ducks might have knocked out Bruin quarterback Nico Iamaleava with a knee injury, but they were destroyed offensively with seven turnovers and just 272 yards of total offense. Oregon is a mess. Star quarterback Dante Moore is expected to miss another game after suffering a concussion against USC. Dylan Raiola might get his shot against his former team, but he was beyond awful against UCLA. Brock Thomas doesn't have Raiola's talent, but he got the offense moving in the second half. Nebraska gave up two huge touchdowns against Indiana, but held firm the rest of the way. Oregon's offensive problems won't all of a sudden be fixed this week. Oct 10, 2026; Lincoln, Nebraska, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea (10) passes against the Indiana Hoosiers during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Why Oregon Will Win Lost in all of Oregon's misery is a defense that showed up and tried to save the day against UCLA. It's been the only team able to stuff the Bruin running game, and it should do the same against Nebraska, starting by keeping quarterback Anthony Colandrea from doing much on the move. The Huskers can force takeaways – three against Michigan State, two against Maryland – but the Ducks are capable of getting their running game moving a bit to take the pressure off the passing game. And about the quarterback situation, yes, Bob Chesney and the UCLA defense pitched a gem last week. But the week before that, Raiola stepped in and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns in a brilliant fill-in performance for Moore against USC. Nebraska vs Oregon Prediction, Betting Lines This is too fluid to be definitive – Oregon might rotate quarterbacks no matter who starts – but this will be more on the Duck defense. It'll be fantastic against the Nebraska running game, and that will be enough. Oregon is 3-0 when allowing fewer than 140 yards on the ground, and Nebraska managed just 128 against Indiana. This won't be pretty, but it'll be a fascinating late-night battle with a few more points than you might expect. picks.headline: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Oregon
picks.blurb: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Oregon - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Auburn stuns No. 1 Georgia A.J. Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Oregon Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nebraska's loss to Indiana last week stung, with the team dropping a 17-6 lead to the defending national champion. Now the Huskers travel up to Oregon for a 10 p.m. CT matchup, the latest start time for Nebraska since 2014. But other factors in this game make this clash all the more questionable. Dante Moore is out for the game, meaning Dylan Raiola, Brock Thomas or even Akili Smith Jr. will be earning the start. But Raiola is the most poetic option after all and is likely the starter despite a rough outing against UCLA. After going 19-of-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, Raiola only threw 6-of-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions against the Bruins . He also got strip-sacked in the game. Though it was Raiola's only sack, UCLA still brought the pressure throughout. Raiola's main weakness is pressure, which the Bruins exploited last week. Though Raiola can find ways to stay alive in the pocket and deliver big plays, he rarely takes off downfield and has found himself in rough spots. Thomas took over in the fourth quarter for the Ducks and went 11-of-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown. He did, however, fumble on his opening drive but nearly completed the comeback. But even if Thomas starts, it remains to be seen whether he can replicate that success, especially after seeing Raiola's two-game stretch. Now, Nebraska can get to the quarterback, but the concern comes down to the explosive plays. Indiana pulled off multiple explosive plays last week, despite its struggle to produce points and yardage for most of the game. The Ducks can do the same, especially late in the game. Nebraska ran out of steam in the fourth against Indiana at home early in the afternoon. Now, the Huskers face Oregon on the road after dark. The Ducks almost completed their 17-6 comeback against UCLA, so they can find a way to do the same against Nebraska if needed. The Huskers' defense also needs to be cautious with Oregon's rushing game. Though the Ducks don't strike primarily on the ground, Dierre Hill Jr. and Jordon Davison combined for 216 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 54 carries over the last two games, averaging four yards per carry. Though UCLA did suffocate Oregon's run at times, Nebraska could let a play slip by if it's not careful. Oregon's defense also needs to be cautious, seeing how its last two games panned out. The Ducks held USC to 27 points, but Jayden Maiava still threw for 326 yards and two touchdowns on just 23 completions. Oregon also surrendered 205 passing yards on just 13 completions to UCLA, despite holding it to 17 points. Nebraska could do some damage on the run, however. Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker tallied 109 rushing yards earlier this season against the Ducks. Anthony Colandrea could do the same and help the Huskers score. Jamal Rule, Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee all could have moments as well after UCLA's Wayne Knight found some holes in Oregon's defensive line. Knight finished with 103 yards on 22 carries. But this game is also make-or-break for Oregon's postseason hopes, especially with Ohio State and even Northwestern coming up. The Ducks also have a talented roster and, despite their issues, can deliver major blows to opponents when momentum is on their side. Nebraska's issues on the line, in the secondary and even a bit on special teams don't help either. All of this, plus the after-dark setting, provides just enough to tip the scales in the Ducks' favor. Unless Nebraska can truly come out and play like a team that can earn a top-25 spot, this matchup will likely be another so-close-but-so-far loss. away.headline: Is Jamir Conn playing against Oregon? Nebraska football injury update
away.blurb: On Friday night, the Huskers released their second-to-last Big Ten Availability report, and Jamir Conn was on it. Conn, a transfer safety who's been one of the team's best defensive backs since arriving in Lincoln, is officially listed as out. He's joined by Rex Guthrie, who is also out and has missed the majority of the 2026 campaign. Senior defensive tackle Riley Van Poppel, who missed Nebraska's game against Indiana, was also listed as doubtful. In the five games he's played this season, Van Poppel has recorded seven tackles and 2.0 sacks. Jamir Conn and Rex Guthrie ruled out as Nebraska football faces Oregon Other Huskers, including Khamir Prescott, Larry Miles, Jase Reynolds, Jacob Bower, and Gabe Moore, have been ruled out since the start of the year. Junior tight end Carter Nelson is the only previously unavailable player no longer listed on the report, so he could see his first game action since Week 3 against North Dakota. Guthrie has battled injuries this season, with his snaps limited to 42, all in nonconference play. But he seemed like a potentially important option, especially with Conn out , given the 574 snaps he logged last year. Guthrie and Conn being out for the game is especially worrisome, as the safety play this season has left much to be desired. Indiana exploited the safety position last week, scoring two fourth-quarter touchdowns over 40 yards, largely because the safeties seemed to misread the plays and didn't provide over-the-top coverage. A 75-yard score, followed by a 44-yard TD pass, both to wide-open receivers, turned a 17-6 Nebraska lead into a 20-17 Indiana win. If there's any good news on the injury front, Oregon has plenty of its own, with quarterback Dante Moore and starting safety Aaron Flowers ruled out earlier this week. Nebraska's safety issues could also be helped by the absence of Oregon's leading receiver Evan Stewart. The wideout was listed as doubtful on both of the last two availability reports . Dante Moore out and Evan Stewart iffy hands Nebraska an Oregon opening it badly needs The Nebraska football team has yet another massive game on its plate in Saturday night's faceoff against Oregon. Unfortunately, the Huskers are not only banged up, but they'll also go into the game without two of their best safeties and one of their best defensive linemen. Conn played just 17 snaps against the Hoosiers but made several key plays before being injured on the first play of the second half. Junior defensive back Caleb Benning replaced the Kansas City-area native for the rest of the game. Benning could be in line for a larger role against the Ducks, though Nebraska defensive coordinator Aurich has emphasized that Nebraska will prioritize getting its best 11 players on the field rather than simply plugging in the next man up. There was some hope that Dante Moore might be able to give it a go this week after returning to practice following his concussion, but the fact that he was ruled "out" in the first availability report, and not even "questionable," is not a great sign for an expedient return. McClellan has been out for a few weeks now after suffering a broken foot in warmups before the Portland State game, and has been seen wearing a walking boot during games. We will see when he is able to get out of the boot and back to practice, but it might still be several weeks, at the least. "He's going to be done for the foreseeable future. Raiola came in of relief of Moore during the USC game and led the Ducks to a win over the Trojans, but Raioa's appearance against UCLA was a different story. Raiola was benched in favor of Thomas in the fourth quarter, and the former third-string quarterback is expected to be thrust into a starting role against the Cornhuskers on Saturday.
